{{nihongo|'''Takaya Shrine'''|高屋神社 (羽曳野市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Habikino|Q694308|qid=Q694308}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Takaya Shrine'''|高屋神社 (羽曳野市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

==Enshrined deities==
It enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}} and Hirokuni Oshitate Kanahi-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ankan|Q241765|qid=Q241765}}).
This area belonged to the lineage of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}, and in ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}'' the “Takaya no Muraji” are recorded as descendants of Ikotone no Ōmuraji, 10th-generation descendant of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto. Thus Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto was enshrined as ancestral deity. Hirokuni Oshitate Kanahi-no-Mikoto was enshrined later.

==History==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded by imperial order in {{ill|538|Q32894|qid=Q32894}} ({{ill|Emperor Senka|Q329728|qid=Q329728}} 3). In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as “Takaya Shrine, Furuichi District, Kawachi Province” and ranked as small shrine, but it does not appear in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=national histories}}.

In the Edo period it was called Hachiman-sha, but in {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} (early Meiji) it was renamed Takaya Shrine, and in {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5) it was ranked village shrine. On May 11, {{ill|1904|Q2046|qid=Q2046}} (Meiji 41), it was {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700}} into {{ill|Shiratori Shrine|Q11580598|qid=Q11580598|lt=Shiratori Shrine}} (Furuichi 1-1, Habikino). In {{ill|1954|Q18581|qid=Q18581}} (Shōwa 29), Takaya Shrine separated from Shiratori Shrine and was restored at its former site, but as of 2018 the deities of Takaya Shrine are still enshrined at Shiratori Shrine as merged deities.
